question: What is the primary purpose of shielding in electrical cables?

options.text: To increase the voltage capacity of the cable
To prevent heat loss from the cable
To increase the current-carrying capacity of the cable
To protect the cable from external electromagnetic interference

solution:
The correct answer is __To protect the cable from external electromagnetic interference****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shielding in electrical cables__ is primarily used to block external electromagnetic interference (EMI).
 
• EMI can disrupt the signals traveling through the cable, causing data loss or corruption.
 
• Shielding helps maintain signal integrity in applications like telecommunications, audio, and video transmission.
 
• It often consists of a metallic layer or braid surrounding the conductors.
 
• Besides EMI protection, shielding also provides some mechanical strength to the cable.
 
• Common types of shields include foil shields, braided shields, and spiral shields.
 
• Shielding is essential in environments with high electromagnetic noise, such as industrial settings.
 
• Proper grounding of the shield is crucial for its effective performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Twisted Pair Cables:**
 
 
• Twisting wires together reduces electromagnetic interference.
 
• Commonly used in Ethernet cables for networking.
 
 
 
• **Coaxial Cables:**
 
 
• These cables have a central conductor, an insulating layer, a metallic shield, and an outer protective layer.
 
• Used in cable television and internet connections.
 
 
 
• **Fiber Optic Cables:**
 
 
• Uses light signals for data transmission, immune to electromagnetic interference.
 
• Ideal for high-speed and long-distance communication.
